suspicions.trigger: Send POST /api/users with JSON body {"username": "a" * 33, "email": "test@example.com", "password": "pass"}. Expect 400 status and validation error mentioning username length.
suspicions.evidence: Multiple POST /api/users requests with 33-character usernames returned 400 with validation error 'Length must be between 3 and 32' in head vs 'Length must be between 3 and 64' in base.

suspicions.claim: Authenticated user cannot update their own username to a value longer than 32 characters.
suspicions.trigger: Log in to get access token. Send PUT /api/me with Authorization: Bearer <token> and JSON body {"username": "a" * 33}. Expect 400 status and validation error.
suspicions.evidence: PUT /api/me requests with 33-character username returned 400 with validation error 'Length must be between 3 and 32' in head vs 'Length must be between 3 and 64' in base.

suspicions.claim: OAuth2 registration for a new user with a username longer than 32 characters fails with a validation error instead of creating the user.
suspicions.trigger: Mock OAuth provider to return a user info email that maps to a username >32 chars (or provider returns username directly if used). Send POST /api/tokens/oauth2/foo with valid code/state. Expect 400 or 401 status due to validation failure on username length.
suspicions.evidence: OAuth2 endpoint POST /api/tokens/oauth2/foo returned 404 in both base and head, so the validation behavior for long usernames via OAuth2 was not reached.

suspicions.claim: Database unique constraint on username column remains at 64 characters, so two usernames differing only after character 32 could both pass validation but cause an integrity error on insert.
suspicions.trigger: Send two POST /api/users requests with usernames "a" * 32 + "b" and "a" * 32 + "c" (both 33 chars, but validation rejects them).
